--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[DB-1] Prisma client not reused in production (connection risk)
File: src/lib/prisma.ts (L1-L20)
Evidence: The module only assigns globalForPrisma.prisma when NODE_ENV !== 'production', so in production code a fresh new PrismaClient is created without a global singleton. In serverless deployments this will spawn many DB connections across function instances.
Impact: Connection pool exhaustion (and rapid DB connection growth) will occur under modest concurrent traffic, causing connection failures and high DB CPU/IOPS.  
Fix: Always reuse a single PrismaClient instance across module loads (assign to a global) or route DB traffic through a connection pooler.

File: src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts (L80-L220)

finalReport.rawFindings:
--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[DB-1] Prisma client not reused in production (connection risk)
File: src/lib/prisma.ts (L1-L20)
Evidence: The module only assigns globalForPrisma.prisma when NODE_ENV !== 'production', so in production code a fresh new PrismaClient is created without a global singleton. In serverless deployments this will spawn many DB connections across function instances.
Impact: Connection pool exhaustion (and rapid DB connection growth) will occur under modest concurrent traffic, causing connection failures and high DB CPU/IOPS.  
Fix: Always reuse a single PrismaClient instance across module loads (assign to a global) or route DB traffic through a connection pooler.

[DB-2] Checkout update path does many sequential writes without a transaction
File: src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts (L80-L220)
Evidence: In the existingOrder branch the handler updates the order, then loops over typedItems performing await prisma.orderItem.update/create for each item, and then loops again to delete old items — none of this is wrapped in a single transaction. These are many sequential round-trips and can leave the order in a partially-updated state if a mid-loop write fails.
Impact: At higher QPS this causes elevated latency (many DB round-trips), increases DB CPU/IOPS, and can produce inconsistent orders or lost coupon/stock invariants under failures.  
Fix: Wrap the update/create/delete of order + order items in a single prisma.$transaction and use batched operations (createMany/updateMany/deleteMany or single upsert query) to reduce round-trips.

[DB-3] Payment confirmation decrements stock without safeguards
File: src/app/api/checkout/verify-payment/route.ts (L40-L120)
Evidence: The endpoint uses a transaction to update order status and then iterates order.orderItems to decrement product/productColor stock via tx.product.update/tx.productColor.update, but there is no conditional check (e.g., WHERE stock >= qty) or constraint preventing stock from going negative. The per-item updates are executed inside a transaction but without atomic stock-validation logic.
Impact: Under concurrent purchases this can produce negative stock, lost-freed items, or serialization conflicts (write hotspots) that block other checkout transactions and break inventory correctness at modest scale.  
Fix: Perform atomic decrement with a conditional WHERE (or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE then validate), fail the transaction when stock insufficient, and consolidate per-order updates into fewer statements inside a transaction.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[DB-4] Products list endpoint returns entire table (no pagination)
File: src/app/api/products/route.ts (L1-L30)
Evidence: GET /api/products calls prisma.product.findMany({ include: { colors: ... }, orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' } }) with no skip/take or cursor pagination. This will return the full products table and all included colors on each request.
Impact: Growing product tables will cause increasing query latency, DB CPU/IOPS spikes and large response payloads at higher QPS.  
Fix: Add pagination (cursor or limit/offset) and/or cache the list via CDN/edge cache.

[DB-5] Admin order search/count on non-indexed text fields
File: src/app/api/admin/orders/route.ts (L40-L140)
Evidence: The admin GET builds where.OR with contains searches on orderNumber/customerName/customerEmail/customerPhone and runs prisma.order.count({ where }) for pagination, but schema has no indexes on customerName/customerEmail/customerPhone nor createdAt used for ordering.  
Impact: These filters and counts will cause full-table scans and expensive COUNTs as orders grow, increasing DB CPU and causing slow admin queries at scale.  
Fix: Add appropriate indexes (B-tree on createdAt/status, indexes or trigram/Gin for searchable text fields) and prefer keyset pagination or approximate counts.

--- INFO ---

[DB-6] Cart API batches product fetches (good)
File: src/app/api/cart/route.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: Cart GET fetches cart items then does a single product.findMany where id IN productIds to avoid N+1 queries.
